crime_highlights: the respondent attacked a jail guard, causing three puncture wounds to his neck
he stabbed his uncle in the neck during a whiskey-fuelled celebration
rationale_highlights: The respondent, an Aboriginal person, grew up in a dysfunctional family.
Both parents physically abused him, and his father sexually abused him.
note: Dangerous offender appeal; appeal court never says Gladue factors reduced culpability.

crime_highlights: J.N.D. was convicted of historic sexual offences against his cousin when she was a young girl.
rationale_highlights: the trial judge was making every effort to apply the principles mandated in Gladue in the face of the options available to her
She was uniquely situated to determine the just and appropriate sentence balance of the societal interests and the moral blameworthiness of J.N.D.
note: Brief deference ruling; no statement that Gladue factors reduced culpability or sentence.

crime_highlights: The appellant was convicted of various offences arising out of the alleged sexual assault of S., his nine-year old daughter.
rationale_highlights: the trial judge did give meaningful consideration to the appellant’s Aboriginal background
note: Appeal court finds consideration adequate; never says background reduced the sentence.
